title: Vilasa 6. The Vision of Rupa and Sanatana; Srinivasa's Initiation
html:
Srinivasa's despair under the tree; Rupa and Sanatana appear to him; the meeting with Jiva at Govinda's temple; Gopala Bhatta; initiation before Radha-ramana and instructions on sadhana

1Glory, glory to Gaurachandra, glory to Nityananda!
Glory to Advaita-chandra, glory to the host of Gaura's devotees!

2Glory, glory to Sri Jahnava, glory to Virachandra!
Those two pairs of lotus feet are my shelter.

3Now hear what I write, O hearers,
you whose life's treasure is the lila of Radha and Krishna.

4To whoever tells and whoever hears, my obeisance.
[Here is] the full account of Srinivasa's state beneath the tree.

5He weeps and rolls on the ground like a mad baul,
crying "Rupa! Sanatana!" and moaning "Alas, alas!"

6"Whatever I long for turns out fruitless;
all the commands given me have proved vain.

7In Purushottama I did not get to see Mahaprabhu;
with the Pandita1 I did not get to read the Sri Bhagavata.

8Sarakara Thakura commanded: 'Go to Vrindavana,
go quickly and see Rupa and Sanatana.'

9Ishvari commanded: 'Go to Vrindavana,
see Rupa together with Sanatana.'

10So Sri Jahnava Thakurani told me.
My life is leaving me — to whom shall I tell this sorrow?

11How many offences have I committed through how many births!
I endure the pain of separation, and yet I do not die.

12Leaving my own land I have come — to Mathura, or where?
I have not seen Vrindavana; my birth has been in vain.

13I would have taken shelter at the Bhatta Gosani's feet,
but in separation from the two Gosanis how can life remain?

14What is the use of going home? I did not get to see them;
my body is in vain — I have not gained shelter at their feet.

15If Srinivasa dies, who will come to see him?
There remains the hope of attaining those feet in another birth.

16Taking refuge in this dharma, how many, many people
float in an ocean of happiness, leaving sorrow and grief behind!

17But all sorrows [fate] has laid upon me;
with what consolation can I console myself? My soul is shattered.

18O Prabhus Rupa and Sanatana, masters of Srinivasa!
I never saw your forms with my own eyes."

19In this way he lies on the ground beneath the tree;
his body is motionless, only breath remains.

20Seeing Srinivasa weeping and crying out,
Rupa and Sanatana came and appeared to him in person.

21"Rise, rise, Srinivasa, look — we are close by;
you are the Prabhu's image of prema, you are my very life.

22All these days I have been watching the road for you —
how can life remain in separation from the Prabhu?

23Why are you turning back, my son? Go to Vrindavana;
may your desire be fulfilled and your longing satisfied.

24Take shelter at the feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta;
know for certain that through him my mercy will come to you.

25I have told Sri Jiva about you;
read the books with him, keep his company."

26He had not slept — Srinivasa rose at once,
and, rising, prostrated himself, offering obeisance and praise.

27Rising, he gazes at their forms, the craving of the eyes;
standing, he beholds the splendour of the two brothers' bodies.

28Their bodies golden and full, a thin shikha on the head,
tilaka on the brow, kanthi beads gracing the neck.

29All over their bodies the two names "Radha" and "Krishna" are written;
over the kaupina an outer cloth is worn.

30They count Hari-nama on the hand, uttering it with the tongue,
and now and then the names of Radha and Krishna sound forth.

31The fragrance of their bodies is like kunkuma and other scents;
the rows of their teeth are lovely as kunda flowers, their smile sweet.

32All sorrow went far away — [there was] an ocean of joy;
Srinivasa's heart became utterly intoxicated.

33His mind overcome with ecstasy, he fell to the ground;
they themselves lifted him and placed their feet on his head.

34Both vanished and went to their own place;
Srinivasa came to outward awareness and reflected in his mind:

35"What more is there to do? Go, my mind, to Vrindavana!
The masters of the masterless are Prabhus Rupa and Sanatana.

36Sri Gopala Bhatta Prabhu is my life;
may Sri Jiva Gosani show me boundless mercy."

37Overwhelmed with feeling, he goes along the road,
not knowing whether it is night or morning has come.

38Meanwhile Rupa and Sanatana themselves commanded Sri Jiva:
"Srinivasa has come.

39In the evening, at the time of Govinda's arati,
he will surely come for darshan.

40Seeing Govinda's form, he will be overcome with ecstasy
and in a frenzy fall on the left side of the doorway.

41When you go for Govinda's darshan at that time,
search for him to the right and left of the doorway.

42Console him and keep him in your own house,
and then take him to Sri Gopala Bhatta,

43so that he may show mercy to Srinivasa;
and you, take him with you and read the books of bhakti with him.

44Teach him those books for the sake of Gauda,
so that people may practise them, abandoning jnana and karma."

45In the same way they went to the Bhatta Gosani
and told him in detail of Srinivasa's coming:

46"He has come to Mathura and today will come to Vrindavana;
he will take shelter at your feet.

47Show him special, boundless mercy,
so that he may go to Gauda with the books of bhakti."

48Having said this, Sri Rupa vanished.
Now I write the account of Srinivasa's arrival.

49Rapt in prema he goes along, dancing as he goes,
walking the road and looking to right and left.

50With his eyes he sees a golden Vrindavana;
with his mouth he says: "Sri Govinda! Gopinatha!"

51He saw the enclosing wall around Govinda's temple;2
at the sight his heart overflowed and could find no rest.

52Streams of tears flow unceasingly from his eyes:
"I shall behold Govinda's lotus feet!"

53Saying this, he arrived there in the evening;
flutes, vinas, pakhawajs and gongs resounded.

54Standing behind the people, he gazes at the form
and sees tears raining from everyone's eyes.

55Prostrating themselves, all went inside,
and Srinivasa came into the jagamohana.3

56He sees Govinda's beauty, with joy in his heart:
as is the form, so are the qualities — just as it was described.4

57Rupa composed an ashtaka5 on what he had seen,
and wove prema into it syllable by syllable.

58Govinda's body surpasses Manmatha himself;
Srinivasa sank into it and found no bottom.

59Rapt in feeling, he lies to the left of the doorway,
and people whisper to one another: what are they saying?

60At this moment Sri Jiva arrived;
prostrating himself, he took darshan of Govinda.

61Many people were with him, carrying lit torches;
the Prabhu's6 command had been given, and his heart was glad.

62He went and saw him lying to the left of the doorway;
sitting down, he calmed him, laying a hand on his body.

63He saw the intense feeling in the depths of his heart,
and with the people took him through the gate to his own house.

64When the second prahara of the night came,
he said nothing; only his throat rattled.

65Then Jiva knew that the ecstasy was coming to an end;
sitting near him, he laid a hand on his body.

66After a while he cried out "Govinda!",
and tears flowed from his eyes, streaming down his breast.

67Sri Jiva asks him: "What is your name?
Tell me, let me hear it; let my heart rejoice."

68Prostrating himself, he gave his name as Srinivasa:
"I was born in a twice-born family; my village is Chakhandi."

69"Friend, friend!" [Jiva] cried, and embraced him:
"Gauranga, the treasure-house of mercy, has brought you to me.

70Such an ocean of compassion I have never seen:
Rupa and Sanatana have given wealth to a pauper."

71The next day, rising, he said: "Listen, Srinivasa:
it is the Prabhu's command — come, go to the Bhatta Gosani.

72Go and take shelter at his feet."
"As you command," said Srinivasa.

73So saying, the two went to the Gosani,
and from afar prostrated themselves.

74"I was born in a brahmana family; my name is Srinivasa;
if you command, I shall take shelter at your feet."

75"Come, come, Srinivasa, come, my son!
How much affliction has fallen upon me in my old age!"

76Approaching his feet, he prostrated himself;
in his mercy he placed his hand on his back.

77Placing his feet on his head, he told him everything:
in separation from the two Gosanis he had suffered great pain.

78"See, in this body of mine only bones are left;
to whom shall I go now for comfort?

79Why have you come so late, my son?
[You were] needed — I would have gone along with you.7

80Why did you not come all this time, Srinivasa?
Everyone hoped to see you."

81"Prabhu, I beg you: forgive my fault.
I had a great longing to read the Sri Bhagavata.

82Because of my fault my heart was troubled;
I went once again to the Pandita Gosani.

83I saw that book — it was in the Prabhu's own hand,
but all the letters were rubbed away, and I was much grieved.

84The Pandita Gosani said to me:
'Bring a new book from Sarakara Thakura's house.'

85With his letter I came to Khanda-grama;
I was given the book and came back to Purushottama.

86While still on the way I heard that the Pandita Gosani had withdrawn from sight;
my heart was stricken and I was in dire straits.

87Then in Navadvipa I saw the feet of Ishvari,8
and with her leave I went to Shantipur.

88At Khardaha I saw the feet of Jahnava;
she commanded: 'Go and see Thakura Abhirama.'

89Everyone commanded: 'Go to Vrindavana.'
All that happened I lay before you, Prabhu."

90Hearing his words, the Gosani wept long
and fell senseless to the ground.

91"My son, you are fortunate, and I am luckless;
for all those faults I suffer so much sorrow.

92I never had the sight of Nityananda's feet,
I never saw Advaita-chandra — my life is fruitless.

93Nor did I ever again see the feet of Ishvari,9
and Sarakara Thakura never once showed me mercy.

94Fate has thwarted all these wishes of mine;
with all these sorrows life will not stay within.

95And now both Rupa and Sanatana have withdrawn;
fate has fashioned my heart out of wood and stone."

96Jiva was present, sitting on his seat.
"Fate has deprived me of everything good.

97I am a sinner: they have all withdrawn from sight,
and through all these separations I cling to this worthless life."

98Srinivasa weeps, fallen at the feet of both;
how many displays of that feeling can I write down?

99In a changed mood Sri Jiva goes to his lodging;
Srinivasa bowed and took his leave [of the Gosani].

100So the two10 remain in the delight of talk about Krishna;
knowing neither night nor day, they float ever in prema.

101A good day and an auspicious hour were calculated,
and Srinivasa went with the Gosani.11

102They took a garland of tulasi manjaris and sandal paste;
carrying them in his hands, Srinivasa followed behind.

103The two came to Sri Gopala Bhatta;
Srinivasa bowed and offered humble praise.

104"Rise, my son; I shall speak — hear the word that is the essence."
Having heard him, Srinivasa spoke again:

105"Mahaprabhu, the guru of the world — the dharma he practised
is all set out in the books of Sri Rupa.

106The instructor is [guru] to the servant birth after birth;
so is the mood of following established — of the follower and the one followed."12

107At that moment Sri Jiva said:
"As you have said, so accept him."

108"Good, good," said the Gosani, and rose quickly,
and went with Srinivasa, joy in his heart.

109To where Sri Radha-ramana disports himself
the two went for darshan.

110Washing their feet, they bowed,
and, prostrating themselves again, entered the temple.

111Knowing the time, Srinivasa bows:
"Come, come, Srinivasa, come near me."

112He sat at the guru's left, facing east,
and with a joyful face beholds the Deity's form.

113Holding his feet, he surrendered himself;
accepting him as his own, the Gosani said:

114"Wash both hands once more,
and with joined palms meditate on the son of the King of Vraja.

115At his left is Sri Radhika, enchanting beyond measure,
and Lalita, the manjaris and others, beautifully adorned."

116He had him worship each of them separately,
offering tulasi manjaris, garlands, sandal paste and the rest.

117Hand to hand he joined them all into their groups,
and made Srinivasa the maidservant13 of them all.

118"Worship Sri Radha-ramana once more,
at whose feet all desires are fulfilled."

119He put fragrant sandal paste on his breast,
and many tulasi manjaris were laid at the [Deity's] feet.

120Placing his right hand on his head, he spoke the Hari-nama,
and then the rule of the five names of Radha and Krishna.14

121Holding both his hands, he imparted the mantra of Radha and Krishna
and let him hear the kama-bija, counting on the fingers.

122"These mantras you will remember
whenever you meditate, taking shelter in her.

123Under the shelter of Guna Manjari you are Mani Manjari;
I shall tell you all about your group.

124Rupa, Guna, Rati, Rasa and Manjulali15 —
these are the companions you are with; they are favourable to you.

125The service follows the bhajana of raga that follows the ragatmika;
the words of Sri Rupa Gosani agree with this.

126"Service" is the name of the sadhaka's great yearning;
when it is perfected, all this is attained.

127The body performs sadhana, and so it is called "sadhaka";
know for certain that perfection lies in the shelter of a sakhi.

128I have named many of the sixty-four limbs of sadhana;
understand clearly what is favourable and what is unfavourable.

129Whatever is unfavourable, reject;
whatever is favourable is the cause of attainment.

130[Guard against] all offences in service and against the Name:
entering the heart, they ruin bhajana.

131The limbs of devotion to Krishna are the attainment through sadhana;16
if one does otherwise, sadhana flies off who knows where.

132The mind fixed on Krishna is the cause of attaining Krishna;
by practising those limbs, attainment is assured.

133Listen, Srinivasa, to how offence arises;
I shall tell and explain it in detail.

134One who does not practise the limbs of bhakti himself and reviles [them],
[…]17

135The banyan seed is tiny, but the tree is enormous —
so offence grows day by day.

136Reviling the gods, causing suffering to living beings and the like —
the heart not drawn to these has bhakti in that measure.

137When you see the scriptures, then you will know;
at that moment you will accept my words as true.

138Having set out on this path, be careful;
bhajana of Krishna — the saints and scriptures are its proof."

139The mercy shown to Srinivasa — in it is all perfection;
fate did not give me a hundred thousand mouths and a hundred thousand ears.18

140He whose hope is the feet of Sri Jahnava and Virachandra,
Nityananda Dasa, tells the Prema-vilasa.

Thus ends the sixth vilasa of the Prema-vilasa.

Notes

  1. Gadadhara Pandita in Puri (see vilasa 4).
  2. Literally "circular enclosure" (cakrabeṛa). This couplet is found only in the 1913 edition.
  3. The jagamohana is the front hall of a temple, before the sanctum.
  4. The line is understood tentatively: Govinda's form is as Rupa described it (see the next couplet).
  5. An ashtaka is a hymn of eight stanzas.
  6. Rupa's and Sanatana's.
  7. The sense of the line is unclear.
  8. Vishnupriya (see vilasa 4).
  9. Here apparently Jahnava.
  10. Srinivasa and Jiva.
  11. Here with Jiva.
  12. The couplet is unclear ("upadeśa kartā sevakera janme janme haya / anugatā anugata bhāvera niścaya"); the rendering is tentative. It is also unclear who speaks, Srinivasa or Gopala Bhatta.
  13. That is, in the spiritual form of a manjari maidservant.
  14. Unclear; perhaps a mantra of five names is meant.
  15. Names of manjaris: Rupa, Guna, Rati, Rasa and Manjulali Manjari ("mañjulāmañjula" taken as "Manjulali Manjari").
  16. A variant in the 1913 edition: "...in them is the attainment of rasa".
  17. The second line of the couplet is corrupt in the 1913 edition and lost in the 1999 edition; it apparently says that such a person attains nothing and his bhajana is ruined.
  18. To describe it. The end of the vilasa (couplets 134–139) is badly damaged in the 1913 edition and is restored from the 1999 edition.
